content.comment_body: Hello everyone, if you read the title you might wonder, is this for real? My issue is that I've written a switching program that seems to run only on [product_name] [version_no], while I only have [product_name] [version_no]. In [product_name] I go to device selection and the [article_no] is set by default. However, I actually have the [article_no] model with a display. When I select the [version_no] model, a red message appears at the top: "The Menu option on the [product_name] start screen is not supported." What do I need to change in my program so it loads onto the [version_no]? I haven't used any features unique to the newer hardware. Thanks!

Hello, This section of the forum operates in English. So you're asking why your program made for [product_name] [version_no] won't download to a [product_name] [version_no]? If you press F2, the Infoscreen will indicate the issue. If you still run into challenges, feel free to upload your zipped program here. Tip: To avoid these problems in the future, make sure you choose the correct [product_name] model (ctrl+H) before starting your work. Regards,
Thank you very much, I'll try asking again in the German section of the forum.

Hello, I think you haven't used any of the new features from [product_name] [version_no]. Device selection in [product_name] provides two options: 1. You can select the hardware ([version_no] in your case) and then, after creating your program, check (F2 & status window) which hardware can handle it. 2. If you know from the start which [product_name] model to use, then pick it during device selection—any functions not supported will automatically be disabled. Feel free to upload your zipped program; we can check it for you. I've found that in [product_name] [version_no], under status text (for message blocks), you can choose a function block. The checker says this should work on [product_name] [version_no], but it doesn't since the [product_name] [version_no] only handles status text via I/O control. Hope this helps. Regards

Hello, I'll close this thread since it is being discussed in the German forum as well. Please remember that our forum has both German and English sections. Make sure to use the language appropriate for each section you visit. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience problems when transferring programs between hardware versions, even if no new features are used. The feedback offered by the software and the limitations imposed aren't always clear or actionable for users, who might expect compatibility across versions. There is a need for more intuitive handling and clearer messages within the software to assist users with cross-version transitions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect software to be compatible between hardware versions when newer features are not used, and want clearer notifications or automatic adjustments when moving programs between [product_name] versions. They seek guidance on what modifications are required to enable compatibility.
